text.title: Risk Assessment Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a decision gate actually consumes the register, whether an owner can be named per row, and whether the draft items are uncertain events scored on one banded scale — to a full register, a fix-before-scoring step, a re-score, or a skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Which decision gate consumes this register — what gets approved, blocked or released on the strength of it?

branch.when: nothing is approved or blocked on the output; it is being produced because a template asks for a risk section

conclusion.verdict: skip: the output would be a scored list nobody acts on, and a well-formatted register is the artefact most likely to be mistaken for risk management happening

branch.when: the decision is one person's and reversible within days

conclusion.verdict: skip: the register costs more than the exposure — write the reversal condition on the ticket instead

branch.when: a gate consumes it, but every candidate owner is a role, a team or TBD

conclusion.verdict: stop and resolve ownership first: rows with no nameable person are removed with a recorded reason, not carried unowned; if that empties the register, skip and escalate the ownership gap instead

branch.when: a gate consumes it and this is the first register for the decision
branch.question: Read the draft list of items as written — what are they?

branch.when: topic nouns such as competition, regulation or hiring, or events that have already occurred with known cost

conclusion.verdict: rewrite before scoring: recast each item as because-of-cause / uncertain-event / leading-to-consequence, and move realised events to the plan as issues

branch.when: genuine uncertain events, but the 1-5 scale is anchored on verbal terms (low / medium / high, likely) with no stated probability bands or time window

conclusion.verdict: fix `matrix` first: one probability band table over one stated window, identical for every row, before any likelihood is entered

branch.when: genuine uncertain events on a banded scale, but consequences land in different currencies — revenue here, reputation there, schedule elsewhere

conclusion.verdict: declare one impact unit (currency of loss, or weeks of runway or schedule) in `matrix` and re-express every row in it; a mixed-unit product cannot order the register

branch.when: uncertain events, one banded window, one impact unit, and a named person per row

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology: score every row on the fixed bands, take the top quartile, and attach an observable trigger plus a dated mitigation and residual score to each

branch.when: a prior register exists for the same decision and a review_cycle date has arrived
branch.question: What would change in the refresh if nobody intervened?

branch.when: prior likelihood and impact would be copied forward because the underlying evidence has not been revisited

conclusion.verdict: re-score every row against current evidence and keep the prior score beside the new one with the re-assessment date; a carried-forward register freezes at its authoring date and readers stop opening it

branch.when: top-quartile rows carry mitigations, but no observable trigger threshold and no due date

conclusion.verdict: attach to each score-16-or-above row a metric crossing a named threshold or a dated external event, a mitigation with a due date, and the residual score after it

branch.when: every row will be re-scored against current evidence, owners are still named, and the band table is unchanged

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology as a re-score: retain prior scores with dates, re-derive the top quartile, and refresh triggers and residuals
